sections.h2: What to weigh before selling a McAllen house
sections.html:
Three things usually decide it: what repairs cost, whether anyone has a claim on the title, and when you need the money. Prices in McAllen are modest next to the Dallas suburbs, so a few thousand dollars in repairs or fees can eat a big slice of the result.

On July 1, 2025 the city was estimated at 150,640 residents, up 5.9 percent from 142,188 in 2020. It is a steady, unhurried rise.

  • An agent opens the door to the most buyers and the longest wait.
  • Selling yourself keeps the fee and gives you the forms.
  • A cash purchase means no repairs and no showings, at a below-retail price.

Among large Texas cities, McAllen sits at the affordable end. Between 2020 and 2024 an owned home had a median value of $190,400, and a household had a median income of $61,579.

sections.h2: Hidalgo County and McAllen's land records
sections.html:
McAllen lies on U.S. Highway 83 in southern Hidalgo County, and that county's offices keep its deeds and tax accounts. The land goes back to Spanish grants of 1767 and the later McAllen Ranch, and the town incorporated in 1911.

Colonias of different sizes surround the city, so a buyer might ask about water, power and lot status. If your lot is out toward the edge of town, keep the survey and utility records close.

sections.h2: Local factors that affect a McAllen sale
sections.html:
Get an inspector's view of the roof, cooling system and drainage ahead of listing. Written repair estimates let you judge offers fairly.

  • Make sure the deed names every current owner, especially when the house moved down a family without probate.
  • Ask the Hidalgo County tax office for the balance owed, earlier years included.
  • Verify homestead, over-65, disability or veteran exemptions with the Hidalgo appraisal district.

English and Spanish are both common in deals here, so a bilingual title officer and translated documents can keep a sale moving.

McAllen wants every short-term rental unit registered annually. A rental is any residential dwelling or accessory building let for less than 30 consecutive days. Paperwork goes to the environmental health and code compliance department at the McAllen Development Center, North 15th Street.

If guests have stayed in your house, a buyer will want proof that the registration is current. The ordinance requires the following:

  • The fee is $100 per unit, and registration runs one year unless ownership changes.
  • Name a local contact who answers the phone at any hour and shows up in person within one hour of a complaint.
  • Each sleeping space needs a working smoke detector, and an exit map has to be posted.
  • A monthly hotel occupancy tax report is due even in months with no bookings.

A violation is a Class C misdemeanor with a fine up to $500, and each day counts as a separate offense. The director can revoke a permit, and the property then waits twelve months to reapply. Since registration does not override private deed restrictions, check any HOA rules as well.

sections.h2: Eviction when a McAllen house has a tenant
sections.html:
The first step is a written notice to vacate, usually three days unless the lease says differently, before the case goes to justice court.

  • A hearing is scheduled between 10 and 21 days after filing.
  • Whoever loses has 5 days after judgment to appeal to county court.
  • The writ of possession is available from day six following final judgment.

A house with a tenant in it can still be sold, and plenty of investors buy such houses. If you need it empty, plan the notice timing before you sign a contract.

In spring, the Hidalgo County Appraisal District mails a Notice of Appraised Value to owners whose market value went up by $1,000 or more. Three numbers appear: market value on January 1, the assessed or net appraised value after limits such as the homestead cap, and taxable value after exemptions.

If you think the market value is too high, file a protest by May 15 or within 30 days of the notice mailing, whichever is later. You can mail it or take it to the district's office on South Professional Drive in Edinburg. Afterward, an online account shows the district's evidence, and an informal meeting with an appraiser follows. Refuse the settlement offer and you go before the Appraisal Review Board, where a family member or friend may represent you with an Appointment of Agent form.

A successful protest lowers the tax bill but not the sale price, because buyers pay what the market bears. It can still reduce the tax split between you and the buyer at closing.

sections.h2: Behind on payments or inherited the house
sections.html: If you close ahead of a foreclosure auction, the equity stays with you and a deficiency suit is avoided. Inherited houses go several ways. A transfer on death deed recorded in the owner's lifetime skips probate, and without it heirs can file a muniment of title or an affidavit of heirship, though buyers can say no to the latter.

sections.h2: Getting a McAllen house ready for buyers
sections.html:
Buyers in the Rio Grande Valley pay close attention to cooling, roofing and how water leaves the lot after a heavy rain. Run the air conditioning before showings, repair any leaks you know about, and make sure gutters and yard grading carry water away from the foundation. These are small jobs next to what a buyer's inspector will notice if they are skipped.

A house that has been in the family for years may also carry old paperwork problems. Look for deeds, tax receipts, utility bills and any survey you have, and sort them into one folder. If the title is unclear because an owner has died, the time to start fixing it is before you accept an offer, not after, since a sale cannot close until the right person can sign.

Once you say yes to an offer, a title company reviews county records for liens, unpaid taxes and gaps in ownership. Houses handed down within families sometimes lack a recorded probate, so this step carries weight in McAllen. Problems it finds get cleared first, and only then do you sign the deed for the county clerk to record.

Have the deed, your latest tax statement and, if you still owe on the house, a payoff letter. A financed sale adds an inspection and appraisal that cash buyers skip, so a cash timeline is often much shorter. Before committing, have the buyer write down the price, closing date and who pays closing costs, and measure that against a listing estimate net of commissions and repairs. If the house has a lease or an unusual lot situation, say so early so the title company can plan for it.

faqs.a: Hidalgo County. McAllen is in the southern part of the county, so Hidalgo County offices handle your deed and tax account.

faqs.q: What is a typical McAllen home value?
faqs.a: The 2020-2024 estimate is $190,400 for an owned home. Repairs, size and age move any single house away from that figure.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited McAllen house without probate?
faqs.a: Sometimes, if the owner recorded a transfer on death deed beforehand. Without one, heirs choose among probate, a muniment of title and an affidavit of heirship.

faqs.q: How fast can a landlord remove a tenant in Texas?
faqs.a: Expect a hearing 10 to 21 days after filing, then a writ of possession from day six after judgment. Appeals have a 5 day limit.

faqs.q: Does selling help if I am behind on my mortgage?
faqs.a: It can, when closing comes before the auction. Proceeds pay the lien first. Ask the servicer for a payoff statement.
